Use case: identity-preserve. Transparent2D fighting-game animation cel strip. Image1 is the ORIGINAL approved idle: exact identity, anatomy/proportions and original rough ink style. Images2 and3 are the AUTHOR-APPROVED LEAD-leg front kick (contact and chamber), reference for face, hair, clothing hues, texture, boot construction and sparse animation style. Now design a kick with the OTHER, REAR leg. Do NOT repeat or mirror that lead-leg kick.
Character: the identical ugly angular boxer, short spiky hair, asymmetrical wrinkled grimacing face, matte dusty maroon-brown short-sleeved T-shirt, same loose muted reddish-brown trousers and heavy dark lace-up boots. Retain original head size, body mass, clothes seams, shoulder/sleeve shapes and dark crosshatching. No handsome superhero face, glossy muscles, saturation boost or new garment colors. Facing SCREEN RIGHT in exactly the reference3/4 camera. Fists keep a compact boxing guard, gaze toward opponent; pelvis, torso and head turn modestly together without throwing head back.
LEG IDENTITY IS CRITICAL: in original idle the boot at screen RIGHT is the FRONT/LEAD leg and stays GROUNDED for both new cels. The leg that originally extends down to screen LEFT is the REAR leg and is the one that rises and strikes toward screen RIGHT. Weight shifts onto the grounded forward boot. Keep that forward support ankle and sole in the same position within both cels, roughly local x280,y523. The rear hip/knee/ankle must remain anatomically connected; no third leg, fused thighs, backwards knee or missing support leg. Both cels must show the SAME rear striking leg. No jump, full spin, leg split or horizontal flip of reference2.
OUTPUT: a single transparent strip with exactly TWO equally sized cells side by side. Ideal canvas1000x550, each cell500x550. Left cel is CHAMBER, right cel is CONTACT. Full-body uncropped figure in each cell, same body scale as Image1, no resizing by pose bounding box. Keep all body, boots and hair12px inside its own cell; supporting sole at y523. Original idle will be reused exactly, do not redraw an idle. No text, labels, panel borders, grids, background, floor, cast shadows, effects or opponent. True transparent alpha.

variants.a-rear-front: VARIANT1: COMPACT REAR FRONT KICK to abdomen. LEFT: transfer weight onto the lead/right-side grounded leg, lift the rear/left-side knee forward to belt height, with rear lower leg tucked under it, front supporting knee slightly flexed. RIGHT: straighten that REAR leg into a solid forward push, boot sole toward screen right and toes up, knee just softly bent. Thrust at abdomen height, not head height. Body stays fairly upright with only a small counterlean. Grounded FRONT boot stays at its original forward support point; the rear boot travels from the back through the chamber to the target. The hip and legs must show clearly that this is the opposite leg to approved reference2.
variants.b-rear-heel: VARIANT2: REAR HEEL DRIVE to ribs with a compact hip turn. LEFT: on the grounded FRONT/lead leg, draw the REAR knee across just in front of the pelvis as a side-kick chamber; subtle chest/hip turn, guard intact. RIGHT: drive that REAR heel toward screen right at waist/lower-rib height, leg almost horizontal and naturally a little bent, toes slightly down, heel leads. Modest coordinated hip/torso rotation makes the thigh seen more side-on; keep the same3/4 camera and identifiable face. This is a rear-leg side thrust, not a spinning back kick. FRONT support boot pivots modestly around its planted forefoot without relocating. Show a strong connected support leg and rear kicking thigh, no stretched femur or huge shoe.
variants.c-rear-round: VARIANT3: REAR ROUND KICK to side of torso, distinct from a straight sole thrust. LEFT: lift REAR knee outward and forward to waist height while FRONT boot remains grounded, shin folded; begin a small coordinated hip turn. RIGHT: swing the REAR shin around toward screen right into an abdomen/lower-rib target. Thigh and shin form a shallow natural knee bend, instep/toes point along shin rather than toes-up front-kick sole. Show a readable roundhouse arc through hip and knee orientation, not special effects. Body inclines only slightly away from target, front supporting knee flexes and its boot pivots around the planted forefoot. Keep the front support foot grounded in the same place and two separate connected legs. No high head kick, acrobatics, sideways neck or whole-body spin.
